hook: Press B4 on a vending machine and you always get the same snack. That one-button, one-snack rule is what makes a function: every input gives exactly one output. Precalculus is the study of functions, so this page sets up the words and notation the whole course uses.

ideas: Function: each input gives exactly one output. $f(3) = 7$ means the input $3$ gives the output $7$.
Domain: the inputs a function accepts. Range: the outputs it produces.
Zero: an input with output $0$, an $x$-intercept of the graph. $y$-intercept: the point $(0, f(0))$.
To evaluate, replace every $x$ with the input in parentheses: $f(-2)$, $f(x + 1)$.

misconception.right: $f(x + 1)$ changes the input: replace every $x$ with $x + 1$. $f(x) + 1$ changes the output: add $1$ after evaluating. For $f(x) = x^2$ they are $(x + 1)^2$ and $x^2 + 1$, which differ.

summary: A function gives each input one output, written $f(\text{input}) = \text{output}$. The domain is every allowed input (no zero denominators, no square roots of negatives); the range is every output. Zeros are inputs with output $0$; the $y$-intercept is $(0, f(0))$. Piecewise-defined functions use the piece whose condition the input meets.
